sections.title: Level 2 Strategy in Statistics
sections.content: In Level 2, the focus is on Variance and Standard Deviation along with Mean. Step 1: Identify the type of data (ungrouped or discrete grouped). Step 2: Calculate the mean or use the given mean. Step 3: Find deviations from the mean. Step 4: Apply the formulas for variance and standard deviation.

sections.title: Concept of Variance
sections.content: Variance shows how widely the data is spread around the mean. Step 1: Calculate the mean (x̄). Step 2: Subtract the mean from each observation (x − x̄). Step 3: Square these deviations. Step 4: Take the average of the squared deviations. Formula: Variance = Σ(x − x̄)^2 / n.

sections.title: Standard Deviation
sections.content: Standard deviation is the square root of the variance. Step 1: Calculate the variance. Step 2: Take the square root of the variance. Step 3: It represents the spread of the data in a simpler form. Formula: SD = √Variance. Example: If variance = 16, then SD = 4.

sections.title: Variance in Discrete Grouped Data
sections.content: Step 1: Identify values (x) and frequencies (f). Step 2: Calculate the mean or use the given mean. Step 3: Compute (x − mean)^2. Step 4: Multiply each result by its frequency. Step 5: Divide Σf(x − mean)^2 by the total frequency.

sections.title: Correcting Mean and Variance
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the total number of observations (n). Step 2: Find the difference between the incorrect and correct observation. Step 3: Adjust the total sum to correct the mean. Step 4: Adjust the squared values for correcting the variance. Example: If 45 was mistakenly recorded as 54, then the difference of 9 must be adjusted in the mean and variance.

sections.title: Properties of Variance
sections.content: Step 1: If a constant c is added to every observation, the mean increases but the variance and SD remain unchanged. Step 2: If every observation is multiplied by k, the variance is multiplied by k^2. Step 3: The SD is multiplied by k. Example: If SD = 5 and every value is multiplied by 3, the new SD = 15.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Calculating the mean incorrectly, which leads to an incorrect variance. 2. Forgetting the squaring step. 3. Not multiplying by frequency in grouped data. 4. Not adjusting incorrect observations properly in correction problems.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Variance measures the spread of data, and standard deviation is its square root. Adding a constant does not change variance, while multiplying by a constant multiplies variance by k^2 and SD by k. In correction problems, the incorrect observation must be properly replaced.

tricks.title: Variance Formula Trick
tricks.explanation: Variance = Σ(x − mean)^2 / n. Take the square of deviations from the mean.

tricks.title: Standard Deviation Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of variance.

tricks.title: Grouped Data Trick
tricks.explanation: Always multiply the squared deviation by the frequency.

tricks.title: Constant Addition Rule
tricks.explanation: If c is added to every observation, variance and SD remain unchanged.
tricks.example: SD = 6, add +5 to all values → new SD = 6.

tricks.title: Multiplication Rule
tricks.explanation: If every observation is multiplied by k, variance becomes k^2 times.

tricks.title: SD Multiplication Trick
tricks.explanation: In multiplication cases, SD is multiplied only by k.

tricks.title: Mean Correction Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Replace the incorrect value with the correct one and adjust the sum.
tricks.example: If 54 should have been 45, subtract 9 from the sum.

tricks.title: Variance Correction Idea
tricks.explanation: In corrections, the squared terms (x^2) must also be adjusted.
tricks.example: Remove 54^2 and add 45^2 in the variance calculation.
